newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.

text.p: COMEX gold and silver futures ended higher Monday, helped by ongoing nervousness about the direction of U.S. stocks and bonds, while NYMEX platinum and palladium closed lower, after news a strike at South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd had ended.

"Gold looks like its still trying to find a bottom, helped by the rise in U.S. interest rates and nervousness about the stock market, but the long downtrend may not be over yet and there's not much fundamental reason to be bullish on gold," Pioneer Futures analyst Scott Meyers said.
COMEX December gold ended up $2.10 an ounce at $332.50, , its highest level since late July, but total COMEX gold volume was light at around 29,000 lots.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid below 8,000 points again intraday as U.S. treasury bonds weakened further, but after COMEX closed the Dow recovered to be up 30 points at 8,8061 near the close of the stockmarket.

"Friday's breakdown in financial markets was quite severe and may not be over yet, but the trade wants to sell gold around $333.00 (basis COMEX December contract)," North American Equity Services COMEX floor trader, John Geraghty, said.
December gold has been in a $320-335 range since early July.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $328.20/70 an ounce, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $327.70 and the New York close Friday around $326.90/40.
Gold mining stocks edged up also, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's index of North American mining stocks (.XAU) at highest levels since mid-June around 102.85 points near the close.

Investor flows into gold and natural resource funds increased to $59 million in the week (ended August 7), following the previous week's increase of $12 million," Salomon Brothers analyst Leanne Baker said.
COMEX September silver ended up 6.5 cents at $4.40 an ounce, as the contract continued to recover from last week's sell off.
NYMEX October platinum ended down $1.70 an ounce at $442.00, NYMEX September palladium lost $2.25 an ounce to close at $222.00 an ounce.

Platinum lost a little ground on news South Africa's Impala Platinum Holdings (Implats), one of the world's largest suppliers of platinum group metals, had settled a seven day old strike with 400 workers at its refineries.
Implats produced about 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months ended December 1996 and normal output is about one million ounces a year.
"The stops have been cleaned out to the upside, and it may take more fundamentals about supply problems in Russia to test the highs again," R.J. Futures NYMEX floor trader, Ralph D'Esposito said.

The August consignment of PGMs from Russia to Japan arrived in Tokyo late last week, but no further Russian spot sales have been noted and lease rates remain high, reflecting the acute shortage of physical metal, traders aid.
One month platinum lease rates remained around 20 percent, while one month palladium rates were around 90 percent.
